behavioral_notes.observation: The `/shop/cart` route (http, public) renders a draft sale.order as the eCommerce cart; `request.cart` IS the cart. `/shop/cart/add` (jsonrpc) calls sale.order._cart_add(product_id, quantity), which first calls _cart_find_product_line to dedupe matching lines (same product_id, uom, no custom attrs, same linked_line/combo) and either bumps the existing line via _cart_update_line_quantity or creates a new sale.order.line via _create_new_cart_line/_prepare_order_line_values (resolving variant via _get_closest_possible_combination + _create_product_variant). Public/anonymous carts are owned by the website public user. Not visible in metadata.

Storefront checkout is a multi-step state machine over one sale.order: /shop/checkout (sets sale_last_order_id, validates cart+addresses, picks delivery via _set_delivery_method) -> /shop/address -> /shop/payment (recomputes cart, lists payment.provider methods) -> /shop/payment/validate (on success calls _check_cart_is_ready_to_be_paid + _validate_order to confirm the order, i.e. transition sale.order to state 'sale', then website.sale_reset()) -> /shop/confirmation. This is the network->chain handoff: the storefront turns an anonymous session into a confirmed sale.order feeding the sale chain. Not visible in metadata.

A draft website cart older than website.cart_abandoned_delay with lines and a non-public partner is flagged is_abandoned_cart (computed + custom _search_abandoned_cart). _filter_can_send_abandoned_cart_mail + _cart_recovery_email_send send the website-specific cart_recovery_mail_template_id (deep-linking back to /shop/cart) via automation, then set cart_recovery_email_sent to avoid resending. A marketing/re-engagement side-effect invisible to metadata.

product.template is extended with website.published.multi.mixin (per-website publish/visibility), website.searchable.mixin (frontend search incl. trigram GIST index on translated fields), website.seo.metadata, and rating.mixin (portal_rating reviews). This is what turns a back-office product into a storefront-published, searchable, rateable catalog item with public_categ_ids, ribbons, images and base-unit pricing. Not visible in metadata.

83 JS files, 6 OWL components, ~38 registry registrations dominated by public.interactions (cart, checkout, dynamic product/category snippets, search modal, recently-viewed, carousels) plus a `cart` service and `cartNotificationService`; 46 entries in web.assets_frontend. The storefront UX is delivered as website public interactions, not backend OWL views.

it_architecture.application: website_sale (eCommerce storefront application component; bridge website->sale)
information_flows: depends: website, sale, website_payment, delivery, portal_rating, digest, website_mail, html_builder
inbound: website (CMS/visitor/public user) -> /shop storefront -> draft sale.order cart
side-effect: /shop/payment/validate -> sale.order._validate_order -> state 'sale' (hands to sale chain -> delivery + invoice)
side-effect: payment.provider transaction (website_payment) confirms cart and triggers confirmation email

value_streams: Browse-to-Order (eCommerce): visit storefront -> add to cart -> checkout/address -> pay -> confirmed sale.order
Confirmed order then enters the sale Quote-to-Cash chain (delivery + invoice)
policies: 6 record rules + 71 ACLs: per-website publish/visibility scoping, ecommerce_access (public/logged-in) gate
metrics: sale.report (with website_id, is_abandoned_cart) eCommerce sales analysis

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_sale is a BRIDGE module: it turns the website value-network (a CMS that mediates between visitors via shared infrastructure) into an order-generating sales channel. It connects website (network) -> sale (chain) -> payment (network): the storefront mediates many anonymous/portal visitors over shared catalog/cart infrastructure (network logic, Stabell & Fjeldstad), and at /shop/payment/validate it calls sale.order._validate_order to emit a confirmed sale.order that feeds the sale chain (delivery + invoice), while website_payment provides the payment-network leg. Its own primary economic activity is the eCommerce sell-side storefront, hence APQC 3.0 Market and Sell (online channel). Classified network rather than chain because its value is mediation/matchmaking and channel infrastructure (publish, browse, search, cart, recover) over a shared platform, not the linear transform-inputs-to-order of the sale chain it feeds. Activity is primary (revenue-facing, customer-facing channel).

standard_capabilities: Public storefront (/shop) with categories, search, ribbons, product pages
Session-based cart on draft sale.order (add/update/clear, anonymous + portal)
Multi-step checkout (address, delivery method, extra info) and online payment
Order confirmation, e-receipt PDF and confirmation email
Abandoned-cart detection and recovery email automation
Cross-selling / up-selling (accessory & alternative products), recently viewed
Per-website publishing, pricelists, currencies and SEO metadata
typical_fits: B2C catalog browse -> cart -> pay -> confirmed order
Multi-website / multi-currency storefronts on one database
Portal self-service reorder of past online orders
common_gaps: Bespoke checkout steps / one-page checkout customization
Complex tax/shipping rules beyond delivery + fiscal positions
Advanced promotions/loyalty beyond pricelists (needs loyalty module)
drive_hints: curl jsonrpc /shop/cart/add {product_id, quantity}  # add a product to the cart (auth=public)

open_questions: Exact sale.order._validate_order semantics vs sale.action_confirm (what downstream stock/account documents are created for an eCommerce order, and when invoicing is automatic).
How the website_payment payment.transaction lifecycle (authorize/capture/error) gates _validate_order and the confirmation email.
Variant-generation path: how /shop/cart/add + configurator routes resolve dynamic/no_variant combinations into the final sale.order.line product.
